deck: NEBLI::UC02::P3::Bio celular e tecidual::Histologia dos vasos

cards.text: Blood flows down a {{c1::decreasing}} pressure gradient: artery → arteriole → capillary → venule → vein.
cards.extra: High pressure + thick wall → low pressure + thin wall.

cards.text: From inside out, the three vessel tunics are the {{c1::intima}} (endothelium), {{c2::media}} (smooth muscle/elastin), and {{c3::adventitia}} (connective tissue).
cards.extra: Same plan in every vessel; local pressure sculpts each layer's thickness.

cards.text: The wavy elastin sheet separating the arterial intima from the media is the {{c1::internal elastic lamina}}.
cards.extra: External elastic lamina bounds media from adventitia.

cards.text: Vasa vasorum (vessels of the vessel wall) are more numerous in {{c1::veins}}.
cards.extra: Venous luminal blood is O2-poor, low-pressure → wall fed worse from the lumen.

cards.text: All vessels are lined by a {{c1::simple squamous}} epithelium sealed by tight junctions: the endothelium.
cards.extra: Aligned to flow.

cards.text: Endothelial {{c1::nitric oxide}} relaxes medial smooth muscle → {{c2::vasodilation}}.
Endothelium secretes {{c1::von Willebrand factor}} → platelet adhesion at vessel injury.
Atherosclerotic plaque begins at the {{c1::injured endothelium}} (hypertension, smoking, cholesterol).
cards.extra: Intima; the thinnest cell of the wall.

cards.text: Which artery type (aorta, carotid) has a media of {{c1::fenestrated elastic laminae}} and buffers the pulse via the {{c2::Windkessel}} effect? {{c3::Elastic artery}}
cards.extra: Stretch in systole, recoil in diastole → pulsatile flow becomes continuous.

cards.text: Which artery type (radial, tibial, splenic) has a media dominated by {{c1::smooth muscle}} and regulates {{c2::caliber}} to distribute blood? {{c3::Muscular artery}}
cards.extra: The media component names the artery.

cards.text: The stain that reveals elastin, separating elastic from muscular artery, is {{c1::Weigert}}.
cards.extra: Elastic laminae as stacked dark lines.

cards.text: Which vessel (< 0.5 mm) sets peripheral {{c1::resistance}}, the main control of arterial pressure? {{c2::Arteriole}}
cards.extra: Wall nearly as thick as the lumen is wide.

cards.text: At the capillary bed entry, the {{c1::precapillary sphincter}} gates flow in waves by local demand.
cards.extra: Short sparse-muscle vessel at the transition = metarteriole.

cards.text: A {{c1::portal}} system passes blood through {{c2::two}} capillary beds in series (hepatic portal vein; renal glomerulus).
The capillary wall is reduced to just {{c1::endothelium + basal lamina}}: no media, no adventitia.
cards.extra: Pericytes outside give support and repair.

cards.text: Which capillary has no pores and a continuous basal lamina (muscle, nerve, connective tissue)? {{c1::Continuous}}
cards.extra: The sealed pattern.

cards.text: Which capillary has endothelial {{c1::pores (fenestrations)}} but a {{c2::continuous}} basal lamina (kidney, gut, endocrine glands)? {{c3::Fenestrated}}
cards.extra: Fast filtration/absorption without losing cells.

cards.text: Which capillary has fenestrated endothelium AND a {{c1::discontinuous}} basal lamina, letting whole {{c2::cells}} pass (liver, hemopoietic organs)? {{c3::Sinusoid}}
Fenestrated vs sinusoid capillary: the discriminator is the {{c1::basal lamina}} (continuous vs discontinuous).
cards.extra: Both have fenestrated endothelium; the endothelium alone confuses them.

cards.text: Which vessel has three tunics under low pressure: no elastic laminae, scant media, thick adventitia, wide lumen? {{c1::Vein}}
cards.extra: Opposite of the same-caliber artery (thick wall, small round lumen).

cards.text: Venous valves are semilunar folds of the {{c1::tunica intima}}; the {{c2::skeletal muscle pump}} drives venous return.
cards.extra: Incompetent valve → reflux → varices.

cards.text: The lymphatic capillary is blind-ended and highly permeable because it {{c1::lacks tight junctions}} (overlapping flaps + anchoring filaments).
cards.extra: Admits fluid, large proteins, and cells that the sealed blood capillary excludes.

cards.text: Lymphatic vessels resemble veins but have many more {{c1::valves}}, since lymph flows with no heart to push it.
cards.extra: Lymph is filtered in nodes, returned via the thoracic duct.

cards.text: The lymphatic system is absent in the {{c1::CNS}}, {{c2::bone marrow}}, {{c3::cartilage}}, {{c4::bone}}, and {{c5::epithelia}} (epidermis, cornea).
cards.extra: Avascular-for-lymph tissues; excess fluid drains otherwise.
